objective: How solid fuels burn in microgravity in a flow duct the first version of this experiment
fuels: Thin and thick flat samples, acrylic spheres, and candles
conditions: Microgravity wind tunnel in the Microgravity Science Glovebox on the ISS with airflow up to 40 cm/s
sensors: Video camera with data overlay and 35-mm still camera
how_it_differs: The original BASS experiment; BASS-II (PSI-25) is its follow-up with more tests and lower oxygen levels
source_notes: Objective and sensor text: BASS-II Summary Report NASA/TM-20210011385 (BASS hardware section) and PSI page
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG), SPICE flow duct
hardware_source: NASA Space Apps 2026, Flame in Freefall challenge notes (Hardware)

investigation: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II
objective: How solid fuels ignite spread and extinguish in microgravity at low airflow
fuels: PMMA film rods and slabs; SIBAL cloth; Nomex cloth
conditions: Oxygen 13.6-22.2% airflow 0 to about 55 cm/s in the Microgravity Science Glovebox on the ISS
sensors: CSA-CP oxygen sensor for oxygen and CO; Carbon Dioxide Monitor for CO2; video camera with data overlay and 35 mm still camera
how_it_differs: Small-scale solid burning in a flow duct; the only investigation in this table with a full public test-by-test CSV
source_notes: Objective and sensor text: BASS-II Summary Report NASA/TM-20210011385 (abstract and sensor sections) and PSI page
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG), SPICE flow duct
hardware_source: NASA Space Apps 2026, Flame in Freefall challenge notes (Hardware)

objective: How a large fire grows in a real spacecraft volume after undocking
fuels: Large fabric sample in an uncrewed Cygnus cargo vehicle
conditions: Large-scale fire in a spacecraft cabin volume in microgravity
sensors: Video and still cameras; temperature and gas sensors in the vehicle
how_it_differs: Full-scale fire growth not small samples; flown on Cygnus not the ISS
source_notes: Objective and sensor text: PSI investigation page summary

objective: How different materials spread fire side by side in a large volume
fuels: Several material samples burned at once in an uncrewed Cygnus vehicle
conditions: Large-scale fire in a spacecraft cabin volume in microgravity
sensors: Video and still cameras; temperature and gas sensors in the vehicle
how_it_differs: Compares materials in the same fire instead of one material per test
source_notes: Objective and sensor text: PSI investigation page summary

objective: How fire spreads in a large volume at a different airflow
fuels: Large fabric sample in an uncrewed Cygnus vehicle
conditions: Large-scale fire in a spacecraft cabin volume in microgravity at a different ventilation setting
sensors: Video and still cameras; temperature and gas sensors in the vehicle
how_it_differs: Same scale as Saffire I with different ventilation; tests how airflow changes large-fire spread
source_notes: Objective and sensor text: PSI investigation page summary

objective: How smoke moves and is detected in microgravity
conditions: Smoke in microgravity with no buoyancy to carry it upward
sensors: Smoke detectors and aerosol sensors; no oxygen sensor
how_it_differs: Detection not burning: it is about finding a fire not measuring how it spreads
source_notes: Objective and sensor text: PSI investigation page summary

objective: Repeat and extend the smoke detection measurements
conditions: Smoke in microgravity with no buoyancy to carry it upward
sensors: Smoke detectors and aerosol sensors; no oxygen sensor
how_it_differs: Reflight of SAME with more runs and conditions
source_notes: Objective and sensor text: PSI investigation page summary

objective: How single fuel droplets burn and go out in microgravity
conditions: Suspended droplets burning in microgravity with controlled oxygen
sensors: Video cameras; temperature and gas sensors
how_it_differs: Gas-phase droplet burning not solid fuels; tests extinction limits
source_notes: Objective and sensor text: PSI investigation page summary
hardware: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) in the CIR
hardware_source: NASA Space Apps 2026, Flame in Freefall challenge notes (Hardware)

investigation: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Burning Rate Emulator
objective: How flammable solid and liquid materials are simulated by burning gaseous fuels under matching conditions
fuels: Gaseous fuels standing in for solid and liquid materials
conditions: Microgravity burning tests in still atmospheres in the Combustion Integrated Rack on the ISS
how_it_differs: Measures flammability by simulation rather than burning the solid itself; one of the ACME family our tables use
source_notes: Objective text: NASA Science investigations page and ACME JASMAC-33 deck (NTRS 20210022542); sensors: ACME chamber instrumentation in the same deck
hardware_source: NASA Space Apps 2026, Flame in Freefall challenge notes (Hardware)

investigation: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame
objective: How diffusion flames behave at the extremes of the fuel dilution spectrum from pure-fuel sooty flames to highly diluted flames near extinction
conditions: Diffusion flames in microgravity with no buoyancy
how_it_differs: Gas flame structure not solid material burning; one of the ACME family our tables use
source_notes: Objective text: NASA Science investigations page and ACME JASMAC-33 deck (NTRS 20210022542); sensors: ACME chamber instrumentation in the same deck
hardware_source: NASA Space Apps 2026, Flame in Freefall challenge notes (Hardware)
